sections.title: Cardiac red flags
sections.alert: Cardiac red flag: treat as an emergency. Record a 12-lead ECG now without delaying transfer, keep the patient under observation and arrange emergency hospital assessment by ambulance; follow the STEMI, NSTE-ACS, acute heart failure, acute aortic syndrome or syncope protocol. A normal ECG does not exclude an acute coronary syndrome.

Chest pain at rest lasting over 15 minutes
ECG: ST elevation, new LBBB or dynamic ST or T wave changes
Syncope on exertion or while lying down
New severe breathlessness, or breathless at rest or lying flat
Sudden tearing chest or back pain
Low blood pressure or signs of shock
Very fast or very slow pulse with chest pain, breathlessness or dizziness

advice.title: Chest pain: when to call an ambulance
advice.text: Call an ambulance or come to the emergency department at once if you get chest pain, pressure or tightness that lasts more than 15 minutes, spreads to your arm, jaw, neck or back, or comes with sweating, feeling sick, breathlessness or fainting. Do not drive yourself.

advice.title: Looking after yourself with heart failure
advice.text: Weigh yourself every morning after passing urine and before breakfast, and write it down. Contact us quickly if your weight goes up over a few days, your feet or legs swell more, you get more breathless, or lying flat makes you breathless. Avoid very salty foods such as pickles, papad and packaged snacks, and do not use salt substitutes or low-sodium salt unless your doctor agrees, because they contain potassium, which can rise to a dangerous level in the blood with some heart medicines or kidney problems. Take your heart medicines every day and stay as active as you comfortably can.

advice.title: Protecting your heart after a heart attack
advice.text: Join the cardiac rehabilitation programme if it is offered. Build up to 20 to 30 minutes of activity every day, enough to make you slightly breathless. Eat more fruit, vegetables, whole grains, pulses and fish, and cook with oils such as mustard, groundnut, sunflower or sesame oil rather than ghee or butter, and avoid vanaspati (Dalda). Stop smoking completely, keep alcohol low, and keep taking your heart medicines; do not stop them without talking to your doctor.

advice.title: If you take a blood thinner
advice.text: Take your blood thinner at the same time every day and do not stop it unless your doctor tells you to. Tell every doctor, dentist and pharmacist that you take it. Come to hospital at once if you have black stools, vomit blood, pass blood in your urine, get a severe headache, or suddenly have weakness of the face, arm or leg or difficulty speaking.
